title: Remove 9
summary: Begin with the integer 1, exclude any number containing the digit 9, like 9, 19, 29, etc.
statement: Begin with the integer 1, exclude any number containing the digit 9, like 9, 19, 29, etc. Generate a sequence: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, ...]. For a given integer n, provide the n^th element in this sequence (indexing starts at 1).
constraints: Return the nth positive integer whose decimal representation contains no digit 9.
hints: The allowed decimal digits 0 through 8 behave exactly like base-nine digits.
Write n in base nine and interpret those digits as decimal.
Repeatedly collect n mod 9, reverse the digits, and parse the result.
Counting strings over nine allowed digits matches positional base-nine counting without ever producing digit 9.
editorial: Counting strings over nine allowed digits matches positional base-nine counting without ever producing digit 9.

tests.explanation: After 1 through 8, decimal 9 is skipped, so the ninth value is 10.
